description: Graded questions over the non-Wikipedia corpora: fifteen Project Gutenberg novels and the ingested TypeScript source tree. Every item names the corpus document that answers it and quotes the supporting text, so a disputed verdict is checkable by a person without running anything. Gold never appears in the item's own prompt, so echoing the question cannot score correct.

corpora.gutenberg: Public-domain novels ingested as evidence spans. Verified present 2026-09-12 by read-only query over sources/source_versions/evidence_spans.
corpora.code: SCCE's own TypeScript tree ingested as evidence spans: 1424 source files, 5231 spans.

kinds: identity: who or what a named participant is
event: what happens at a named point
narrative-relation: a relation that holds between participants inside the text
module-behavior: what a named function or module does

questions.prompt: What does deriveClosedClassWords derive its word set from?

support.quote: Closed-class words (function words, connectives) derived from the active language's evidence, never from a hardcoded list: the most frequent unigrams of the resident Kneser-Ney models plus single-token literal slots of learned constructions.

questions.prompt: In code-request.ts, why are short language aliases like "go" and "js" not counted on sight?

support.quote: Distinctive names identify a language on sight; short aliases ("go", "c", "js") are ordinary words in prose and only count once other code structure corroborates them.

questions.prompt: What does replan reuse instead of redoing it?

support.quote: Reuses every completed node whose own preconditions and claimed postconditions are *not* touched by the observation -- real completed work is never redone just because something unrelated changed.
